Rashi on Nedarim 63b:1:1.english: And it is taught [in a baraita] - [This is] a support.

Rashi on Nedarim 63b:1:2.hebrew: הכותב עד ר"ח אדר - סתם, עד ר"ח אכר הראשון קאמר. מדקתני אם היתה שנה מעוברת וכו', מכלל דרישא דקתני עד ר"ח כו' לאו במעוברת עסקינן? בתמיה! הא מדקתני עד אדר הראשון, מכלל דבמעוברת עסקינן, ומאי שנא רישא ומאי שנא סיפא:
Rashi on Nedarim 63b:1:2.english: One who writes, "Until the New Moon of Adar" - [When stated] without specification, it means until the New Moon of the first Adar. Since [the baraita] teaches, "if it was a leap year, etc.," does that imply that in the first clause, which teaches "until the New Moon [of Adar], etc.," we are not dealing with a leap year? [This is asked] in astonishment! Surely, since it teaches "until the first Adar," it follows that we are dealing with a leap year! So what is the difference between the first clause and the latter clause?

Rashi on Nedarim 63b:2:1.hebrew: אלא שמע מינה רישא דלא ידיע דמיעברא שתא - וכי נדר, לשם אדר הסמוך לשבט קאמר, הילכך עד אדר הראשון. וסיפא מיירי בדידע דשתא מעוברת היא, דהכי משמע: אם היה יודע שהשנה מעוברת, אסור עד ר"ח אדר השני:
Rashi on Nedarim 63b:2:1.english: Rather, learn from it [that] the first clause [refers to a case] where it is not known that the year is a leap year - And when he vowed, he meant the Adar adjacent to Shevat; therefore, [he is forbidden] until the first Adar. And the latter clause deals with [a case] where he knew that the year is a leap year, for this is what it implies: if he knew that the year was a leap year, he is forbidden until Rosh Chodesh of the second Adar.

Rashi on Nedarim 63b:3:1.hebrew: שלא נתכוון זה שלא לשתות אלא עד שעה שדרך בני אדם לשתות יין - דודאי רוצה הוא לשתות ד' כוסות של יין בלילי פסח, שכל אדם שותין:
Rashi on Nedarim 63b:3:1.english: That this [person] intended not to drink only until the time when it is customary for people to drink wine - For he certainly wants to drink [the] four cups of wine on the nights of Passover, when all people drink.

Rashi on Nedarim 63b:4:1.hebrew: אלא עד לילי צום - עד אותה לילה שיצום למחר, ואותה הלילה מותר לאכול בשר:
Rashi on Nedarim 63b:4:1.english: Only until the night of the fast - Until that night [before] he will fast the next day, and [on] that night it is permitted to eat meat.

Rashi on Nedarim 63b:4:2.english: Until the time when it is customary for people to eat meat - And he wants to eat with them.

Rashi on Nedarim 63b:4:3.english: Until the night of Shabbat - And on the night of Shabbat, [it is] permitted.

Rashi on Nedarim 63b:4:4.english: When it is customary for people to eat garlic - And that is the eve of Shabbat.

Tosafot on Nedarim 63b:1:1.hebrew: והתניא - בניחותא. מכלל דרישא לא במעוברת? בתמיה! הא ודאי במעוברת איירי, דהא קתני "עד אדר ראשון"! אלא ודאי במעוברת, וקשיא רישא אסיפא. אלא רישא — דלא ידע דמעוברת, סיפא — דידע דמעוברת ונדר עד אדר שני; וקאמר דאדר סתם של מעוברת היינו אדר שני, דחדש העיבור אדר ראשון הוא ולא אדר שני. תדע, שהרי אדר הראשון משלשים יום, שני מכ"ט. ועוד, דמגילה ופורים בשני, אלמא ראשון חודש העיבור:
Tosafot on Nedarim 63b:1:1.english: And it is taught - [This is read] as a statement [rather than a question]. Does [this] imply that the first clause is not [referring] to a leap year? [That is] astonishing! For surely it is speaking of a leap year, since it teaches "until the first Adar"! Rather, it is certainly [speaking] of a leap year, and [thus] the first clause contradicts the latter clause. Rather, the first clause [refers to] where he did not know that it was a leap year, [and] the latter clause [refers to] where he knew that it was a leap year and vowed until the second Adar; and [the baraita] is saying that an unspecified "Adar" of a leap year is the second Adar, because the intercalated month is the first Adar and not the second Adar. Know [that this is so], for the first Adar consists of thirty days, [and] the second of twenty-nine. And furthermore, [the reading of] the Megillah and Purim are in the second [Adar]; thus, the first [Adar] is the intercalated month.

Tosafot on Nedarim 63b:1:2.hebrew: עד ר"ח אדר הראשון - דסתם אדר הוא אדר הראשון:
Tosafot on Nedarim 63b:1:2.english: Until the New Moon of the first Adar - Because an unspecified Adar is the first Adar.

Tosafot on Nedarim 63b:3:1.hebrew: שלא נתכוון זה אלא עד שדרך בני אדם לשתות יין - דהיינו עד לילי הפסח, דבליל פסח יש לנו לומר שלא אסר עצמו:
Tosafot on Nedarim 63b:3:1.english: That this [person] intended only until [the time] when it is customary for people to drink wine - That is, until the nights of Passover, for on the night of Passover we must say that he did not forbid himself [from drinking wine].

Tosafot on Nedarim 63b:4:1.english: Until it will be the fast - [That is,] the fast of the tenth [of Tishrei, i.e., Yom Kippur].

Tosafot on Nedarim 63b:4:2.hebrew: עד לילי הצום - דהיינו סעודה של יום הכפורים, דרגילין לאכול בשר, כדאיתא בחולין (דף פג.): "רבי יוסי הגלילי אומר: אף ערב יום הכפורים בגליל":
Tosafot on Nedarim 63b:4:2.english: Until the eve of the fast - That is, the meal [on the eve] of Yom Kippur, when [people] are accustomed to eat meat, as it is stated in Chullin (83a): "Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says: Even [on] the eve of Yom Kippur in the Galilee."

Tosafot on Nedarim 63b:4:3.hebrew: שדרך בני אדם לאכול שום - דהיינו ליל שבת, שהוא מתקנת עזרא שיאכלו שום בע"ש:
Tosafot on Nedarim 63b:4:3.english: "When it is customary for people to eat garlic" - That is, Shabbat night, for it is from the enactment of Ezra that they should eat garlic on Shabbat eve:
